correctness.rationale: Independence and closed-neighborhood domination yield unique fiber states and node runs; explicit transitions give the rational bivariate series. The optimum-count proof checks full-fiber exceptions via a sharp integer inequality, then counts run compositions and colors. Positive irreducible weighted transitions with aperiodic F–F loops give a unique analytic pole; two unequal-length F–F cycles prove the variance is strictly positive. Independent direct graph/word/transfer checks were run for 13 cases (403264 original graph masks); finite checks are not substituted for general proofs.

originality.rationale: Relevant 2018–2022 open-access primary literature and targeted research-index/web searches were compared by implication. The 2019 Kuenzel–Rall weak-partition characterization already supplies the fiber criterion, and the 2022 result already supplies the minimum cardinality. Neither inspected quantitative result states the present rational complete enumerator, exceptional exact optimal multiplicities, or Gaussian limit. General feasibility does enable deriving the result and carries a documented residual equivalence risk.
residual_risks: Published weak-partition criteria give a strong general membership characterization from which enumeration can in principle be deduced; closely equivalent counts may exist under a different notation.
An unindexed enumerative paper or OEIS table could contain some exact coefficients or recurrence.
Not every publisher-formatted version of the 2019 article was directly inspected; the accessible complete HTML rendering was used.

value.rationale: A complete all-size distribution and residue-wise optimum multiplicities answer natural questions left open by knowing only the smallest possible set. The Gaussian law with strictly positive variance and exponentially vanishing optimum fraction quantify how typical maximal independent sets differ from optimized ones in a canonical graph-product family. The contribution is more than a renaming, a table replay, or a routine finite computation.
